request: Average across all segments; clarify what a point represents
statistic: DTW distance, not transformed similarity; lower means more similar
aggregation: Existing same-word/same-phone-position comparisons -> mean within each English speaker -> equal mean over six English speakers -> mean within L2 word/type -> equal mean over word types within L2 speaker/phone -> equal mean over all available phone types within L2 speaker -> equal mean over L2 speakers within L1
small_dot: One L2 talker, averaged over all their eligible phone types
large_dot: Equal-weight mean of L2 talker averages within L1
diamond: An L1 group with one L2 talker; no group CI
ci: 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles; resample talkers within L1 with replacement; references and within-talker means held fixed; no CI for n=1
weighting: Equal phone-type weighting, not interval-frequency weighting; all eligible types, not only previously displayed types
limitations: Unbalanced available phone and word coverage; no missing type filled with zero
Automatic target-conditioned boundaries are not human-verified
Strict duration/posterior filtering leaves 197 intervals and is not used in this primary plot
Not a formal L1-effect test, whole-word distance, GLMM, or three-fold CV result
